comparable_cases.why_comparable: Immediately adjacent address (906 Clement St, next door to 910), Type 41 ABC license for restaurant with full cooking, approved 2016 in the Inner Clement NCD.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Type 41 for the restaurant immediately next door (906 Clement) was approved within 28 days as an agency referral. Planning required the operator to 'operate as a Bona Fide Eating Place'—a standard ABC condition—but imposed no other restrictions despite the already dense concentration of licenses on this block.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 40 meters away at 852 Clement St, Type 41 ABC referral for restaurant, same zoning district (NCD-INNER CLEMENT), decided 2022.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Type 41 approved at 852 Clement within 11 days in 2022 with no conditions beyond the standard 'Bona Fide Eating Place' requirement and compliance with Planning Code Section 202.2(a)(1) location and operating controls. Demonstrates routine approval pattern continues on this block.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Same address as above (852 Clement St), Type 41 ABC referral one year earlier, approved 2021.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Prior Type 41 approval at 852 Clement in 2021 within 10 days, described as 'continuation of an existing use.' Shows Planning treats Type 41 licenses for restaurants in the Inner Clement NCD as permitted uses requiring only ABC and health department coordination, not discretionary review.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 100 meters away at 800 Clement St, Type 41 ABC referral for non-formula restaurant, approved 2022 in the Inner Clement NCD.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Type 41 approved within 14 days at 800 Clement in 2022 with no conditions. Planning's description emphasized 'non-formula retail restaurant use,' confirming that independent restaurants with beer-and-wine are principally permitted and processed as routine agency referrals in this district.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 57 meters away at 832 Clement St, limited restaurant (DPH referral), approved 2021 in the Inner Clement NCD.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Limited restaurant at 832 Clement approved within 35 days in 2021 as a DPH referral with no Planning conditions. Confirms that even new food-service establishments without prior use history are approved quickly in this corridor when zoning-compliant.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 235 meters away at 4724 Geary Blvd, Type 41 ABC referral for restaurant in the adjacent Geary Boulevard NCD, approved 2023.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Type 41 approved in 2023 within 98 days (longer than Inner Clement cases) at Geary Boulevard with standard 'Bona Fide Eating Place' and Section 202.2(a) controls. Slightly longer timeline may reflect workload variation, but no additional neighborhood-specific restrictions despite Geary's similar density.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 208 meters away at 315 8th Ave, conditional use authorization for restaurant expansion with existing Type 41 license, filed 2020 and withdrawn 2022 in the Inner Clement NCD. This is a use decision record, not an agency referral.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The only discretionary use decision within 1,000 feet in the last decade was a CUA for a restaurant expansion (merging two tenant spaces). The applicant withdrew after two years; the record does not state why, but the fact that a straightforward beer-and-wine restaurant operating in one space avoids CUA review entirely highlights the difference between principally permitted and conditional uses.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 67 meters away at 939 Clement St, conditional use authorization to intensify restaurant use (add 24 seats on ground floor), approved 1990 in the Inner Clement NCD. This is a use decision record.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This 1990 CUA approval for restaurant intensification (adding seats) predates the current Planning Code framework. Under today's Code Section 716, first-story restaurants with beer-and-wine are principally permitted and do not trigger CUA review, showing that the regulatory path has simplified for standard restaurant concepts.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 94 meters away at 823 Clement St, full restaurant (DPH referral) approved 2019 after 3-year closure for seismic upgrading, in the Inner Clement NCD.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Full restaurant at 823 Clement approved within 29 days in 2019 despite three years of inactivity. Planning treated it as a continuation of a legal non-conforming use rather than a new establishment, showing flexibility for restaurants resuming operations after tenant improvements or closures.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 272 meters away at 4601 Geary Blvd, Type 41 ABC referral for restaurant in the Geary Boulevard NCD, approved 2021.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Type 41 at Geary Boulevard approved within 19 days in 2021 with standard 'bonafide eating place' condition per Section 202.2. Geary Boulevard NCD has similar density to Inner Clement, and approvals follow the same expedited agency-referral pattern for beer-and-wine restaurants.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm the missing inputs with the applicant and Planning before filing or paying any fees.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The rules set the zoning, alcohol and building rows to insufficient information because the description does not give whether the business is part of a chain, the square footage, how the liquor licence will be obtained, what the space was last used as, the occupant load, or the existing occupancy group. Confirm those answers in writing with the applicant, then submit them to Planning's information desk or the Permit Center to settle the zoning and building answers before filing. If the space is under 2,500 square feet, not a formula retail chain, and was last used as a restaurant or food service, the use is principally permitted and no conditional use authorization is needed. If any answer triggers a conditional use (formula retail or over 2,500 square feet), file a pre-application meeting request with Planning before signing the lease or paying application fees.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State and obtain an EIN from the IRS.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File LLC Articles of Organization (LLC-1) or corporation articles with the California Secretary of State online; the fee is $70 for an LLC or $100 for a corporation. File the Statement of Information within 90 days ($20 for an LLC, due every two years). Then apply for an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS online; it is issued immediately and free. The EIN and entity name are needed for the bank account, the lease and the liquor licence.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Register for a California seller's permit with CDTFA and a San Francisco business registration certificate with the Treasurer & Tax Collector.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online with the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) for a seller's permit; it is free and often issued the same day. ABC will not issue a liquor licence until the seller's permit exists, so do this early. Then register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer & Tax Collector within 30 days of starting business in the city; the fee is tiered by gross receipts (e.g. $55 up to $100k, $625 at $1–1.5M for 2026–27). Every other city department asks for the Business Account Number (BAN), so register immediately after forming the entity.

filing_playbook.action: Submit DPH plan check for the kitchen build-out at the same time as the building permit application to DBI.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Any new food facility or remodel affecting the kitchen needs DPH approval of plans, finishes, equipment and menu. The 2026–27 flat fee is $2,207 for a new restaurant (8 hours), with extra review at $276/hr. Coordinate with your architect to submit both applications at the same time. After approval, schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% complete and a final inspection, booking each with your plan reviewer at least two weeks ahead.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Install a grease interceptor and submit the Installation Verification Form to SFPUC under the Fats, Oils & Grease (FOG) program.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Under the FOG Control Ordinance every food service establishment that cooks must install grease-capturing equipment; SFPUC inspectors assign a Discharger Category (1–3) that dictates the device type, and new restaurants must install it before opening. Submitting the Installation Verification Form earns a 14.2% reduction on the sewer portion of your bill. An undersized or missing interceptor is a common reason DBI withholds final sign-off. Coordinate with your plumber and the building permit review.

filing_playbook.action: Schedule Fire Department inspections for the commercial kitchen hood and place of assembly (if occupant load is 50 or more).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Commercial cooking hoods need a suppression-system plan review and inspection routed with the building permit. If the occupant load is 50 or more, obtain a Place of Assembly permit from the SFFD Bureau of Fire Prevention ($446, 49 South Van Ness Suite 560) and a posted occupancy sign. The Entertainment Commission also requires this permit for venues of 50+. Schedule the final fire inspection before the DPH pre-opening inspection.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

timeline_cost.notes: The time and cost shown are for the one approval the rules could decide: the health permit to operate. The health permit is issued 14–45 days after plan check and inspection, at a cost of $470–1,000 in government fees (2026–27 schedule). This is a time to approval, not to a denial or a withdrawal. The rules set the zoning, alcohol and building rows to insufficient information, so no timeline or cost is given for those approvals until the missing inputs are confirmed. Once the applicant confirms whether the business is a chain, the square footage, how the liquor licence will be obtained, what the space was last used as, the occupant load, and the existing occupancy group, the rules can decide whether a conditional use authorization, an ABC Type 41 licence investigation, or a building permit with change of occupancy applies. If the use is principally permitted (non-chain, under 2,500 square feet, first story) and the space was last used as a restaurant with no change of occupancy, expect the ABC Type 41 to take 60–120 days and the building permit 14–120 days, with combined government fees of roughly $3,000–18,000 depending on construction valuation. If a conditional use authorization is required (formula retail or over 2,500 square feet), add 120–300 days and $3,100–15,000 for the Planning Commission hearing.
timeline_cost.verification_note: The record covers only the health permit; statements about other approvals, ABC licenses, building permits, and conditional use authorization timelines are not in the cited catalog entry.

records_summary: 910 Clement St sits in the Inner Clement Street Neighborhood Commercial District where a restaurant serving beer and wine is principally permitted on the first story with no conditional use authorization required. The site history shows continuous restaurant use with Type 41 ABC licenses dating back to at least 2005, most recently as a bakery/limited restaurant approved in 2020. The block is densely saturated with food and beverage operations: 17 registered food/drink businesses within 500 feet, 11 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 feet (27 within 1,000 feet), and ABC's undue-concentration flag is triggered. The Inner Clement NCD has seen only routine agency referrals approved in recent years; the one dated use decision within 1,000 feet in the last decade was withdrawn.
